newsitem.title: UK: Bahrain opposition says scores arrested.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain opposition says scores arrested.

text.p: Bahrain's security forces have arrested scores of Shi'ite Moslems in a crackdown against government opponents, an exiled Bahraini opposition group said on Wednesday.

The Bahrain Islamic Freedom Movement said 31 people from various areas had been detained in the Gulf Arab state the past seven days, including Ghalib Ali Hammad, 16, from the Shi'ite village of Jidhafs.
The group said in a statement that police had also detained and later freed Hussain Ali al-Saudi, 11, from Bilad al-Qadeem.
Fires gutted two shops in Bilad al-Qadeem last week causing damage but there were no reports of casualties.
A series of fires hit Bahrain, the Gulf's banking and financial centre, in the past 10 days and government officials said some of them were premeditated.
Shi'ite Moslems have launched sporadic attacks since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.
